title: Fishy starter aquascaping catalog
scope: 20 sourced starter references: 10 aquarium-wood trade types/styles and 10 plant taxa/cultivars.
modelingPolicy: Visual and geometry values are proposed procedural approximations for Fishy, not scans, botanical simulations, or material-identification claims. Wood trade names are supplier labels and must not be interpreted as exact species identities. Source facts are retained only where the opened source states them.

geometryConvention.status: Non-executable art-direction suggestions. No Fishy runtime currently consumes these values, so each two-number array is a suggested visual interval rather than an implementable min/max contract.
geometryConvention.localAssetSpace: All unlabelled linear geometry controls use normalized local asset units (NLU): a generated asset is authored inside a unit bounding box, with 0 at its local origin and 1 spanning its chosen authored extent. NLU values are proportions for visual composition only; they are not centimetres, metres, tank dimensions, or biological measurements.

controlMeaning.twoNumberArray: Suggested lower/upper art-direction interval, not a guaranteed range.
controlMeaning.linearKeys: Keys naming radius, length, height, width, spread, footprint, scale, thickness, depth, radius, or spacing use NLU unless their key ends in Deg.
controlMeaning.ratioKeys: Keys naming density, taper, twist, roughness, contrast, coverage, asymmetry, straightness, exposure, translucency, erosion, massiveness, darkness, lightness, or similar visual qualities are unitless 0–1-style proportions; values outside 0–1 are intentional only where the key is an aspect ratio.
controlMeaning.countKeys: Keys naming count, nodes, modules, forks, lobes, or patches are suggested integer instance counts.
controlMeaning.angleKeys: Keys ending in Deg are degrees in local asset orientation.
controlMeaning.categoricalKeys: String or string-array values are suggested modes/orientations, not enum definitions.

geometryConvention.physicalDimensions: Published plant size and care remain only under each plant's care object (for example heightCm/reportedHeightCm) and are explicitly sourced. They must not be used to scale procedural controls without a future, documented conversion layer.

entries.name: Spider Wood

source.facts: Thin, twisted, light-coloured, branchy root-like structure; retailer says it is typically Azalea or Rhododendron roots.

entries.identityNote: Trade label only; the supplier's 'typically' wording is not a species identification for an individual asset.
entries.visualForm: Pale, fine, multi-arm root crown with long tapered tips.
entries.placementUse: Use as a high-detail focal root or miniature tree canopy; mount moss or small epiphytes only after the actual piece is secured.
entries.safety: No visual safety inference. Verify the purchased item's aquarium-use documentation, preparation instructions, dimensions and edges.

entries.name: Manzanita Aquarium Driftwood

source.facts: Supplier describes sandblasted aquarium pieces with coarse texture, a blondish colour, and variable lengths/diameters; recommends soaking before use for buoyancy and tannins.

entries.identityNote: Manzanita is a trade/common name; this catalog does not resolve an individual piece to a botanical species.
entries.visualForm: Blond, clean, coarse-textured branch or stump silhouette.
entries.placementUse: Use a solitary fork or an assembled grove for a dry-tree silhouette and strong negative space.
entries.safety: No safety conclusion from colour or form; source and prepare the specific aquarium product.

entries.name: Mopani Wood

source.facts: Listing describes a two-colour African hardwood and directs users to soak natural wood products to reduce tannin discolouration.

entries.identityNote: Mopani is retained as the supplier product label; no species-level identification is asserted.
entries.visualForm: Heavy dark-brown and tan, knuckled mass with chunky forks and grooves.
entries.placementUse: Low-to-midground anchor, cave-like mass, or dark contrast against fine-leaved planting.
entries.safety: No safety conclusion from the asset appearance; follow the named product's preparation guidance and verify livestock compatibility.

entries.name: Cholla Wood

source.facts: Retailer identifies it as a dead cholla-plant skeleton with many holes and a hollow centre; says it is softwood that eventually breaks down in an aquarium.

entries.identityNote: The source establishes a cholla-plant skeleton, but no exact botanical species is claimed here.
entries.visualForm: Open tubular cactus skeleton; perforated lattice with a hollow core.
entries.placementUse: Nano-scale hollow accent or shrimp-scale cover; cluster several short tubes as a porous lattice.
entries.safety: Use an aquarium-sold, prepared item only; the visual model does not certify a cactus skeleton as aquarium-safe.

entries.name: Red Moor Wood

source.facts: Supplier describes fine branches, protruding limbs, pre-assembled sets, variable sinking time, and possible brown water coloration.

entries.identityNote: Supplier trade name only. Other retailers may apply Spiderwood/Fingerwood to similar-looking material; do not merge identities from appearance.
entries.visualForm: Reddish-brown, tangled fine limbs radiating in several directions.
entries.placementUse: Layer modules into a tangled thicket or overhang; reserve negative space in front for a readable silhouette.
entries.safety: No inferred safety. Source notes variable sinking and coloration; verify the actual product and preparation.

entries.name: Malaysian Driftwood

source.publisher: Bulk Reef Supply / Ultum Nature Systems
source.facts: Retailer describes dense driftwood with dark rich colour, rugged texture, and a usual tendency to sink without pre-soaking; it suggests soaking or boiling to reduce initial tannins.

entries.identityNote: Regional trade name; no individual wood species or origin chain is inferred.
entries.visualForm: Dark, rugged, dense driftwood with thick organic texture and irregular shelter-like voids.
entries.placementUse: Foundation piece for a dark riverbank, root wall, or planted midground structure.
entries.safety: Do not infer safety from dark colour or density; use a documented aquarium product and inspect/prepare the actual piece.

entries.name: Talawa Wood

source.facts: Aquasabi's driftwood guide characterises Talawa as strongly textured, often relatively straight, lighter under remaining bark, and more streamlined than Moorwood or Red Moorwood.

entries.identityNote: Trade style, not a botanical determination.
entries.visualForm: Streamlined, pale-to-barked linear root with pronounced grain.
entries.placementUse: Directional wood for current- or stream-oriented layouts; align several pieces on one flow axis.
entries.safety: Trade form is not a safety guarantee. Verify aquarium suitability and treatment of the purchased item.

entries.name: UNS Ghost Wood

source.facts: Supplier describes light-coloured driftwood with robust branches/offshoots for freshwater aquariums; each pre-assembled piece is unique and not pre-soaked.

entries.identityNote: Product trade name; no species identification is asserted.
entries.visualForm: Very light robust branch network, coarser and more architectural than fine root wood.
entries.placementUse: Open-layout focal structure; a good host form for moss or epiphyte instances in the visualizer.
entries.safety: Only this named freshwater product is documented by the supplier; appearance alone does not establish safety for substitutes.

entries.name: Dragon Wood

source.facts: Aquasabi lists Dragon Wood as a pre-assembled natural wood with a distinctive hole structure, partial sinking, and slight water coloration.

entries.identityNote: Trade style only; 'Dragon Wood' does not specify a botanical species.
entries.visualForm: Gnarled trunk with irregular, eroded holes and knotted protrusions.
entries.placementUse: Textural midground focal piece; use the cavities as visual planting pockets, not as claims about real plant attachment.
entries.safety: No appearance-based safety claim. Confirm the exact retailer product, preparation, and sharp-edge suitability.

entries.name: Ancient Juniper Wood (procedural layout model)

source.facts: Tropica's Layout 114 names ancient juniper wood as decoration and describes hardscape whose wood tilt follows stream flow.

entries.identityNote: A layout label, not a supplier material specification or a botanical chain-of-custody claim.
entries.visualForm: Weathered, directional conifer-like branch/root silhouette oriented with a flow line.
entries.placementUse: Directional stream composition: orient primary limbs and companion stones along the same current axis.
entries.safety: This is an inspiration/layout reference, not purchasing or safety documentation. Verify any real juniper-labelled wood separately.

entries.name: Micranthemum tweediei 'Monte Carlo'

source.facts: Creeping, compact, round light-green leaves; Tropica lists carpeting, 3–5+ cm, medium light and medium CO2.

entries.visualForm: Fine bright-green round-leaf carpet on creeping stems.
entries.placementUse: Foreground lawn; source also describes use as an epiphyte when wedged into hardscape.
entries.nameNote: Cultivar name retained exactly as supplied; render is not species-accurate.

entries.name: Anubias barteri 'Petite'

source.facts: Tropica calls it a cultivation mutation, under 5 cm tall with very small leaves and a 5–10+ cm rhizome; listed slow, 3–5+ cm, low light and low CO2.

entries.visualForm: Dense miniature deep-green oval leaves along a creeping rhizome.
entries.placementUse: Attach to shaded wood/rock faces; do not visually bury the rhizome.
entries.nameNote: A named cultivation mutation; no broader taxonomic claim beyond the supplied name.

entries.name: Vesicularia ferriei 'Weeping'

source.facts: Tropica describes broad fronds with distinctive downwards/drooping new shoots; it attaches best to wood/rock and says its drooping form needs more light and CO2 than some mosses.

entries.visualForm: Dark-green, fine-frond drapes that hang below a branch or ledge.
entries.placementUse: Thinly attach to branch undersides and vertical hardscape for a canopy/woodland effect.

care.lightCo2: Source says more light and CO2 than some mosses are needed for the distinctive drooping form.

entries.nameNote: Trade cultivar/common-name styling follows the grower source.

entries.name: Bucephalandra pygmaea 'Bukit Kelam'

source.facts: Source says it branches densely without trimming; wavy green leaves are about 2 cm wide and 5 cm long. Tropica lists slow, 5–10+ cm, low light and low CO2.

entries.visualForm: Low wavy-leaf rhizome clump with scattered tiny pale submerged-leaf dots.
entries.placementUse: Attach to wood or rock in the midground; keep visual rhizome exposed.
entries.nameNote: Quoted locality/cultivar label is retained; it is not a generated botanical identity.

entries.name: Alternanthera reineckii 'Mini'

source.facts: Tropica calls it a miniature compact, slower-growing version; trimming can produce a 5–10 cm red-violet carpet. Listed medium growth, 5–10+ cm, medium light and medium CO2.

entries.visualForm: Compact red-violet opposing leaves forming a low trimmed shrub/carpet.
entries.placementUse: Foreground accent in large layouts or compact colour block in small aquariums.
entries.nameNote: Cultivar; a compact red-violet, opposite-leaved stem model is an approximation, not a colour guarantee.

entries.name: Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Green'

source.facts: Tropica states green leaves, 10–30 cm height and 8–15 cm rosette width; listed medium growth, low light and low CO2.

entries.visualForm: Grounded green rosette whose leaves can lie close to the substrate in open space.
entries.placementUse: Midground rosette grouping, especially under larger plants or wood shade.

entries.name: Eleocharis pusilla 'Mini'

source.facts: Tropica says it forms a dense carpet from small planted portions, with 3–5 cm leaves; listed slow, medium light and medium CO2.

entries.visualForm: Short, fine, upright-to-gently-curved grass blades in a dense lawn.
entries.placementUse: Foreground/nano carpet and narrow seams between rocks.
entries.nameNote: Cultivar label from source; generated blades are procedural.

entries.name: Fissidens fontanus

source.facts: Tropica describes a featherlike, tight deep-green moss, relatively slow-growing, suitable for vertical or horizontal attachment; lists 3–5+ cm, medium light and medium CO2.

entries.visualForm: Tight, featherlike deep-green tufts with orderly frond rows.
entries.placementUse: Small crisp patches on wood or rock where a structured moss texture is needed.
entries.nameNote: Species label is source-provided; procedural fronds are only a visual proxy.

entries.name: Glossostigma elatinoides

source.facts: Tropica calls it one of the smallest aquarium plants (2–3 cm) and a foreground plant; source states high light and CO2 promote growth, and lists high light/high CO2.

entries.visualForm: Very low, fine bright-green creeping carpet with tiny rounded leaves.
entries.placementUse: Unshaded foreground carpet; protect the visual area from taller plant overlap.
entries.nameNote: Species source is direct; carpet model is not a botanical simulation.

entries.name: Bolbitis heudelotii

source.facts: Tropica describes translucent green fern leaves, 15–40 cm tall/wide, best planted on root or stone with its rhizome uncovered; lists slow, 15–30+ cm, medium light and medium CO2.

entries.visualForm: Long, translucent green, lobed fern fronds from a horizontal rhizome.
entries.placementUse: Midground/root-mounted fern on a large branch or stone, with exposed rhizome.
entries.nameNote: Species label is source-provided; generated leaf anatomy is a procedural visual approximation.
